Version 0.4.0 adds explicit per-folder direction policies: `send-receive` (the existing default), `send-only`, and conservative `receive-only`. For an authoritative source with a receiving copy, use send-only on the source and receive-only on the receiver. Either device can initiate the connection. The peers negotiate direction on every lane, and local checks enforce it before sending, receiving and publishing changes.

Receive-only never sends indexed changes upstream. Local receiver edits are preserved and can conflict with later source changes; this is not forced mirroring. Changing direction does not discard files, rewrite causal history or resolve pre-existing conflicts. `ysync folder mode ID MODE` requires the daemon to be stopped and holds its lock. New folders support `folder add --mode`. The Ratatui dashboard and JSON status show direction and distinguish disabled sending from successful delivery.

Correctness coverage now includes source/receiver-initiated connections, metadata and bulk lanes, accidental receiver edits, restart/deletion, incompatible modes, opposite directions on separate folders, cancellation before publication, protocol-5 rejection and deterministic mixed offline edits across repeated process crashes. Repeated benchmark tooling uses distinct seeded contents, retains raw samples and records latency/CPU limitations. README and validation documentation now distinguish released capabilities and historical evidence. Controlled competitor comparisons, long-duration testing and application-consistent database snapshots remain open.

**Breaking wire change: protocol 6 requires upgrading both peers together.** Stop both services, run `brew update && brew upgrade ysync` on each machine, then restart them and reopen monitors. Cargo users can install tag `v0.4.0`. Existing folder modes default to send-receive, and identities, configuration, indexed history, conflict archives and resume state are retained. Set any desired direction policies while the daemons are stopped. Experimental prerelease.
